_comment: Every key the Python generators put into a payload the app reads, and what
happens to it on the other side (#262).
Why this file exists: the app decodes only the fields someone remembered to
wire up. `stopped_reason` was written on every halt and read by nothing, and
because the write really did run it looked alive to every is-this-used check
(#257). The sweep that followed found eight more, including OCR's `other`,
which Claude was asked for on every program and which generate_blog has a
prompt slot for that always rendered '(none)'.
The rule this file enforces:
- the Python side's real key set, read from the source by
tests/bridge_payload_keys.py, must equal this file's key set exactly.
A key Python gains fails until somebody declares what happens to it.
- every key marked `swift` must be read on the Swift side, proved by
PostRollApp/Tests/BridgePayloadContractTests.swift.
- a key that is deliberately not read by Swift is marked `python_only`
WITH A REASON. There is no third state: an orphan cannot sit here
unexplained, which is the whole point.
Two kinds of Swift side. `model` names a Codable type, and the guard
populates it, encodes it, and decodes it back, so deleting a line from
init(from:) fails. `reader` names a function that pulls keys out of a
dictionary by hand, and the guard feeds that function a payload carrying
every declared key and asserts each one comes back out. Both prove the key
is READ, not merely mentioned: a reader that keeps values generically
(parsePreviewDayEntry keeps any string that is an existing file) satisfies
this by behaviour without naming a single key, which is the point.

week_result._what: One event week's captions and blog, written after every day so a kill keeps what finished.

week_timing._what: Per-phase durations, feeding the rolling-mean estimate on the generation screen.

run_progress._what: Which step a long run is on, polled by the app so a working run is distinguishable from a dead one.

day_caption._what: One day's caption, hashtags and alt text.

skipped_photos.python_only: generate_week hoists this onto the week payload's `warnings`, which is where the app reads it and where it can be shown per day. DayCaption deliberately does not carry a second copy: two homes for one fact is how it goes missing in exactly one direction (L83).

blog_output._what: The blog post, plus what the deterministic checks caught.

revised_caption._what: A caption after a plain-English revision request.

revised_blog._what: A blog post after a plain-English revision request.

swapped_blog._what: A blog post rewritten around a different set of photos.

ocr_result._what: Structured program data read off the scanned pages.

flag_review._what: Claude's reply in the OCR correction conversation, plus any patch to apply.

media_result._what: The week's rendered graphics, keyed by day, plus per-day failures.

media_day._what: One day's rendered assets. A mix of plain path strings and nested objects.

friday_clip_plan._what: Friday's clip selection: which clips, in what order, trimmed where.

friday_clip_selection._what: One clip inside the Friday plan, already renamed into Swift's field names.

cover_result._what: A single day's regenerated cover image.

swap_reel_audio._what: The result of swapping a reel's audio track without re-encoding video.

meta_import._what: Instagram posts parsed out of Meta's CSV export.

learn_suggestion._what: One brand-voice rule inferred from the edits Dan made to generated text.
